lesson.arabic-headlines-leads.title_en: Reading headlines: a verbal noun, and what it leaves out
lesson.arabic-headlines-leads.family_en: How headlines save words, and the words for the people who write the news

table.form_en: a verbal noun as a headline

steps: Headlines save words. They often use a verbal noun instead of a verb, and leave out who, when and where: اِفْتِتَاحُ مَعْرِضٍ لِلْكِتَابِ, opening of a book fair.
Read a headline as the promise of a story: the first paragraph usually fills in who, where and when.
Don't fill a gap yourself. If the report names no one, it may say only جِهَةٌ رَسْمِيَّةٌ, an official body.
Tell a stated fact from a question or someone's claim: a headline in quotation marks reports what someone said.

examples.en: An accident on the motorway (literally "the happening of an accident").

examples.ar: قَالَ مُرَاسِلُ الصَّحِيفَةِ إِنَّ الْحَادِثَ وَقَعَ صَبَاحًا.
examples.en: The newspaper's correspondent said the accident happened in the morning.

examples.ar: شَارَكَ فِي الْمَعْرِضِ أَكْثَرُ مِنْ مِئَةِ دَارِ نَشْرٍ.
examples.en: More than a hundred publishers took part in the fair.

why.q_en: Why اِفْتِتَاحُ, a noun, and not the verb اِفْتَتَحَ, in a headline?
why.a_en: A verbal noun names the event without saying who did it or when, which saves words. The report under the headline adds what the noun leaves out.

selftest.q_en: The headline says وُقُوعُ حَادِثٍ. What does it tell you?
selftest.why_en: The verbal noun names the event only. The report adds the rest.
A newspaper is صَحِيفَة, and a participant مُشَارِك.

lesson.arabic-news-language.title_en: Who says so: news verbs (أَعْلَنَ, أَفَادَ, نَفَى) and the passive
lesson.arabic-news-language.family_en: Verbs that say where a claim comes from, and how strongly
steps: News says who a claim comes from, and each verb has its own strength: أَعْلَنَ, announced, officially; أَفَادَ, stated; رَجَّحَ, thought likely; نَفَى, denied.
بِحَسَبِ, according to, names the source of a claim: بِحَسَبِ الْوِزَارَةِ, according to the ministry.
The passive leaves out who did it: يُرَجَّحُ, it's thought likely; أُعْلِنَ, it was announced. Don't add a doer the text doesn't give.
In a summary, keep the verb's strength: "announced" and "thought likely" aren't the same.

examples.en: The council announced the opening of a public park.
The official denied there was any delay.

examples.ar: يُرَجَّحُ أَنْ تَنْتَهِيَ الْأَعْمَالُ فِي الصَّيْفِ.
examples.en: The work is expected to finish in the summer.

why.q_en: Why يُرَجَّحُ, with u and a, and not يُرَجِّحُ?
why.a_en: The vowels make it passive. يُرَجِّحُ is "he thinks it likely"; يُرَجَّحُ is "it's thought likely", with no one named. Without the marks the two look the same, so the sentence decides.

selftest.why_en: The other two report what someone said: "announced" and "stated".
مَصَادِر are sources, and مُطَّلِع someone who knows the inside story.

selftest.q_en: Which is the passive, "it was announced"?

lesson.arabic-numbers-data.title_en: Numbers in the news: اِرْتَفَعَ, اِنْخَفَضَ, فِي الْمِئَةِ
lesson.arabic-numbers-data.family_en: Rises and falls, rates and averages, and what a figure needs to mean anything
steps: A figure means little without its unit, its starting point and its period: rose to what, from what, since when?
اِرْتَفَعَ, rose, and اِنْخَفَضَ, fell, take مِنْ for the start and إِلَى for the end: اِرْتَفَعَ عَدَدُ الطُّلَّابِ مِنْ خَمْسِينَ إِلَى سِتِّينَ.
"Per cent" is فِي الْمِئَةِ, "in the hundred". A rate going from 40 to 50 per cent rises by ten points, but by a quarter of what it was.
ضِعْف is double: ضِعْفُ الْعَدَدِ, twice the number. مُتَوَسِّط is an average.
Write an important figure down, with its unit, before you interpret it.

examples.ar: اِرْتَفَعَ عَدَدُ الزُّوَّارِ إِلَى مِلْيُونٍ هَذَا الْعَامَ.
examples.en: The number of visitors rose to a million this year.

examples.ar: اِنْخَفَضَتْ نِسْبَةُ الْبِطَالَةِ إِلَى سَبْعَةٍ فِي الْمِئَةِ.
examples.en: The unemployment rate fell to seven per cent.

examples.ar: بَلَغَ مُتَوَسِّطُ الْأَسْعَارِ ضِعْفَ مَا كَانَ عَلَيْهِ.
examples.en: Average prices reached double what they were.

why.q_en: Why اِنْخَفَضَتْ, with ـَتْ, in اِنْخَفَضَتْ نِسْبَةُ الْبِطَالَةِ?
why.a_en: When the verb comes first, it matches the gender of its subject, the noun right after it: نِسْبَة is feminine, so اِنْخَفَضَتْ. With عَدَد, masculine, it's اِنْخَفَضَ الْعَدَدُ.

selftest.q_en: How do you say "ten per cent"?
selftest.why_en: "Per cent" is فِي الْمِئَةِ, "in the hundred".

selftest.q_en: A rate goes from 40 to 50 per cent. By how many points did it rise?
selftest.why_en: Ten points; as a share of where it started, that's a rise of a quarter.

phrases_ar: اِرْتَفَعَ عَدَدُ الطُّلَّابِ مِنْ خَمْسِينَ إِلَى سِتِّينَ

lesson.arabic-interview-notes.title_en: Notes from an interview: who said what, and how sure
lesson.arabic-interview-notes.family_en: The words for an interview, and how to note a claim with its limits
steps: Keep three things apart in your notes: the question, the guest's answer, and your own reading of it.
Note a claim with its example and any limit the guest puts on it: "in my experience" belongs beside the claim.
Keep "not yet" as "not yet": لَمْ يَصِلِ الضَّيْفُ بَعْدُ, the guest hasn't arrived yet, isn't "he isn't coming".
A quotation, اِقْتِبَاس, must be the exact words: check its صِيَاغَة, wording, against the recording.
If the guest dodges a question, note that it wasn't answered, not what you guess the answer was.

examples.ar: سَأَلَ الْمُحَاوِرُ الضَّيْفَ عَنْ مَوْقِفِهِ مِنَ الْقَرَارِ.
examples.en: The interviewer asked the guest about his position on the decision.

examples.ar: قَالَ الضَّيْفُ إِنَّ الْفِكْرَةَ نَجَحَتْ فِي تَجْرِبَتِهِ الشَّخْصِيَّةِ.
examples.en: The guest said the idea had worked in his own experience.
The guest dodged the second question.

why.a_en: تَهَرَّبَ means to dodge or slip away, and like هَرَبَ, to escape, it takes مِنْ before what you avoid: تَهَرَّبَ مِنَ السُّؤَالِ, he dodged the question.

selftest.why_en: A quotation must keep the exact words.

selftest.q_en: The guest says "in my experience". Where does that go in your notes?
selftest.why_en: Without it, a personal view can look like a general one.

lesson.arabic-news-digest.title_en: A news digest: keeping sources, dates and doubts
lesson.arabic-news-digest.family_en: Words for updates, conflicting accounts and what isn't confirmed

table.en: as he put it, in his words

steps: A digest picks the main points from several sources and groups them by topic, not source by source.
Keep each point's source and date: a later تَحْدِيث, update, may change an earlier report.
Where sources disagree, keep both: رِوَايَاتٌ مُتَنَاقِضَةٌ, conflicting accounts.
Mark what isn't settled: غَيْرُ مُؤَكَّدٍ, unconfirmed; عَلَى حَدِّ قَوْلِهِ, as he put it.
Link the points in your own words rather than pasting sentences.

examples.ar: أَفَادَ التَّحْدِيثُ الْأَخِيرُ بِأَنَّ الطَّرِيقَ مَفْتُوحٌ.
examples.en: The latest update said the road is open.

examples.ar: مَا زَالَ عَدَدُ الْمُشَارِكِينَ غَيْرَ مُؤَكَّدٍ.
examples.en: The number of participants is still unconfirmed.

examples.ar: اِرْتَفَعَتِ الْأَسْعَارُ بِالْمُقَارَنَةِ مَعَ الْعَامِ الْمَاضِي.
examples.en: Prices rose compared with last year.

why.q_en: Why غَيْرَ, with -a, in مَا زَالَ عَدَدُ الْمُشَارِكِينَ غَيْرَ مُؤَكَّدٍ?
why.a_en: مَا زَالَ is a sister of كَانَ, so the describing part takes -a. Here that part is غَيْرُ مُؤَكَّدٍ, so غَيْر takes the -a, and مُؤَكَّد keeps the -in it always has after غَيْر.

selftest.why_en: A later update may change an earlier report.

selftest.q_en: What does عَلَى حَدِّ قَوْلِهِ show?
choices: that these are his words, not the writer's
selftest.answer: that these are his words, not the writer's
selftest.why_en: It keeps the claim with the person who made it.
